correctness.rationale: For n>=5 elementary 4-cycles intrinsically identify local coordinate directions and bound the origin stabilizer by the eight signed swaps. Stable counting colors determine walk counts from the unique landmark; from these determine distance and geodesic count, while equitability determines numbers of predecessors. In Cartesian cycles d=a+b, predecessor count equals 1[a>0]+1[b>0]+epsilon(a)+epsilon(b) and geodesic count equals binomial(a+b,a) times 2 to the number of even antipodes. For odd n and for even n>=6, strict binomial monotonicity plus a p=2 antipodal-axis exception separates all unordered pairs. The orbit upper bound matches the eight explicit signed coordinate maps; all class-size formulas follow. Boundary n=4 excluded. Direct counting tests n=5..70, independent formula/BFS tests n=5..500 or n=5..30, and rooted automorphism tests n=5..7 corroborate but are not infinite proof.

The triple (distance, predecessor multiplicity, shortest-path multiplicity) is an intrinsic small certificate encoded by 1-WL, with a genuine even-cycle antipodal collision issue distinguished uniformly.
